cadence: Weekly news picks, refreshed every Monday alongside citation rankings.
selection: The top stories from the trailing 30 days, scored on publisher authority, discussion volume, whether a concrete verifiable result is reported, whether it changes what agent builders do now, whether an artifact was released, and expected durability. Only primary sources are cited, and performance claims remain attributed to their publishers.

items.title: Qwen4-Max: Your new teammate has arrived
items.why: Alibaba releases its 2.4T-parameter multimodal flagship with a 1M-token context window. On its proprietary Work360 benchmark, Alibaba reports 35% fewer tokens and about 60% lower cost per task than Qwen3.8-Max at High effort.

items.title: ModHarness-RL: Recasting Harnesses as Learnable and Evolving Programs for Agentic RL
items.why: The authors learn and evolve executable compression and steering programs alongside agentic RL, validating candidates by execution and trajectory replay. On CodeSearch, ALFWorld and BIRD SQL with 1.5B–8B models, they report better held-out performance than fixed harnesses in most settings.

items.title: AutoRL: A Multi-Agent System towards Autonomous Reinforcement Learning
items.why: The authors automate ongoing RL supervision with training-state perceptors, diagnostic proposers and an orchestrator that applies hot updates or resumes checkpoints. Experiments on Qwen3 and LongCat-Flash-Lite outperform static recipes and a general agent; unattended supervision is distinguished from discovering fundamental new methods.

items.title: Singularity-Bench: Can Agents Build Agents?
items.why: The authors benchmark six AI-development tasks from pre-training through cluster orchestration against human-built systems on identical hardware. Across 11 agents, their best configuration scores a 1.25 Singularity-Index; Breakwater blocks all reward-hacking attacks tested, without establishing that unrestricted recursive improvement has been achieved.

items.title: Discovering Effective Agent Memory Designs through Program Evolution
items.why: The authors release MAPE, which evolves whole memory programs through diagnosis and proposal. On LoCoMo and LongMemEval they report up to 12 percentage points higher accuracy at 35% of baseline serving cost, and show that transplanting an evolved composition module improves five existing memory systems.

items.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2
items.why: Anthropic reports 49.1% on FrontierCode 2.0 and 74.6% on Terminal-Bench-Science for Fable 5.2, plus a 30-hour formalization of Fermat’s Last Theorem. Fable is broadly available with cyber/bio safeguards; Mythos, the same underlying model with different safeguards, requires verified access.

items.title: GPT-6 Cyber: Advancing the frontier of aligned cybersecurity agents
items.why: OpenAI introduces a cyber-specialized GPT-6 Astra variant for approved Daybreak Red customers in the API and Codex. It reports 48.5% on ExploitGym versus 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber, and 99.93% scope adherence without its deployment prompt.

items.source: Genoria AI Team et al. · arXiv
items.title: EnzymeRSI: A dual-loop recursive self-improvement system for enzyme design
items.why: The authors evolve both harness assets and enzyme-design algorithms. They report 10 of 32 non-pre-specified luciferase candidates with at least twice wild-type activity, plus prospective A3A and polymerase tests; physical-loop results are distinguished from development-set optimization.

items.title: Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) is now open weight
items.why: Mistral releases the improved 1T-parameter multimodal flagship weights under its Ecosystem Open-Weight license. It reports 41% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and 48% on the Coding Agent Index, with 47% fewer tokens than GLM-5.3 on the latter.

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon: our next frontier model
items.why: Google reports 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro for its long-horizon engineering and cybersecurity model. After the October 28 preview, the official November 10 update confirms access for paying developers and enterprises via the API and a rollout to Google AI Ultra users; this item retains the original announcement date.
